title: intentd serves /estate/status: watches the estate directory outside the ingest path, renders the live top-styled page with the host census
objective: intentd answers the estate over the one shell document: the page's data call `{"op":"form","view":"/estate/status"}` returns `result: estate_status` carrying the reader's `intent/estate-status@1` JSON, /estate/status is a route in `shell.html` fed by `/op`, and the daemon renders no HTML for it (D56). The page is live and top-styled, laid out as the attached `estate-status-mockup.html` hv approved on 2026-10-24: one band across the top (the host block, the last hour as sparklines of the 1-minute load and the running slots, plan usage), then the queue, the lanes and the sessions, every panel a native `<details>` whose collapsed summary keeps a live one-line reading; it polls the reader every few seconds while open, so there is no watcher in this package and D20 keeps its two events. The daemon measures the host census itself on its tick: the load averages, one row per declared process class counting running processes attributed to the project whose tree holds each process's working directory, and a history ring; the classes are declared with `intent estate watch <class> <pattern>` and `intent estate unwatch <class>` as `census/watches/<class>.json`, nothing is built in, and the tick reaps gone sessions' WIP records (vc decision 73). Plan usage comes from the account's usage endpoint first, read through Claude Code's own Keychain item under Claude Code's own naming condition with no fallback between names, once per census tick after a status ask, and from `intent estate statusline` second, which a statusline step feeds the JSON it was handed (`printf '%s' "$input" | intent estate statusline || :`), printing `wrote:` on stderr and nothing on stdout; every failure is named in `usage.error`, never silent. `intent estate status --browser` opens the page. Decision 75: the rows of `estate status` are flat, and `watch`, `unwatch` and `statusline` are withheld from MCP with their reasons on the dispatch rows.
